t: You're looking at numbers two and four Redington Road, a pair of nineteenth-century semi-detached houses in Frognal, in Camden. They were designed by Philip Webb. Webb is sometimes called the Father of Arts and Crafts Architecture. He believed in what he called the art of common building, drawing on vernacular tradition. He worked with William Morris, Edward Burne-Jones and Dante Gabriel Rossetti, and he co-founded the Society for the Protection of Ancient Buildings.
